title: A learned gastric-expression score associates with recorded survival
summary: An autoencoder-derived expression score was associated with survival in archived gastric-cancer cohorts and a TCGA comparison. The score used learned transcriptomic features followed by survival regression. The result does not establish a new stem-cell identity, treatment response or a clinically deployable risk threshold.
ai_technology: One-class logistic regression; autoencoder neural network

source_review.scope: Original selected computational/data Methods and represented cohort/physical Results; laboratory/sample preparation procedures excluded

evidence.ai_role: One-class logistic regression derives a source-defined stemness index. A trained autoencoder learns nonlinear expression features subsequently selected and combined with Cox survival modeling, enabling the represented score-outcome association.
evidence.tested: Five expression datasets containing 1,051 samples were split 4:1 for model development and internal assessment. The source reports survival separation in both subsets and in TCGA, where each cohort was divided at its own median score.
evidence.unknown: Discovery preprocessing and stemness-feature selection can reuse cohort information; an untouched fixed-threshold test is not established. The text mentions nine selected prognostic features but displays a five-feature formula; full final coefficient selection remains unverified because the primary supplementary workbook was inaccessible. No reconstruction of the trained model was performed. Treatment-response extrapolations, inferred immune states and the cell-population identity claim are excluded.
